thread:
dave_acme: Hey team — our customers are seeing much worse tail latency on streaming responses after the March deploy. TTFB for the first chunk is fine (~180ms) but p95/p99 total time jumps to multiple seconds, usually ~4–8s. Happening for chat endpoints only (model: gpt-large-open-2026), same requests non-streaming return in ~300–400ms. Trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d. Anyone seen chunk pacing / coalescing regressions recently?

alice_support: Thanks for the callout, Dave. Can you paste a minimal curl repro and the request_id from headers? Also which region and whether the customer is on Dedicated or Hosted?

dave_acme: Hosted, us-west-2. Example curl they used (sanitized):

```
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-open-2026","prompt":"summarize...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```

Response headers had `x-request-id: rwd-abc123` and `x-route: chat-gen-1`

alice_support: perfect. Pinging infra and runtime: @bob_sre @carol_runtime @eva_product — severity = p95 regressed for production customers.

bob_sre: I'm pulling traces for rwd-abc123. Initial server-side generation stream shows tokens emitted quickly, but there's a ~200–400ms gap between first and second chunks in multiple traces. On the network side we see the downstream (edge -> envoy -> runtime) had no obvious retransmits. Potential culprits: proxy buffering or runtime changed flush timer.

carol_runtime: I dug into runtime logs around the March deploy (deploy-bot: 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC). We changed batching heuristics and increased `batch_flush_delay_ms` from 50 -> 200 to reduce micro-batching overhead. That reduces cost but increases inter-chunk spacing for streamed outputs when generation is small bursts. The first chunk is flushed immediately (TTFB OK) but the runtime waits for either more tokens or the flush timer to fire for subsequent chunks.

bob_sre: Also saw edge config bumped `envoy.http2.initial_stream_window_size` in a recent infra change to optimize multiplexing. That shouldn't add ms-level pauses, but combined with runtime timer it can change how chunk sizes map to network frames.

alice_support: Good finds. Customer is asking for mitigation ASAP. What can we do short-term?

carol_runtime: Short-term mitigations we can do from runtime side (low risk):
- restore `batch_flush_delay_ms` to 50 for chat-gen routes (targeted service-level rollout)
- enable `flush_on_first_token=true` (already on, but we can also `flush_on_subsequent_small_chunks=true` so small token groups flush immediately)
- add an immediate flush after we observe generation end-of-turn marker (if present)

I can prepare a canary config that applies only to the hosted chat-gen pool.

bob_sre: From infra side:
- temporarily set `envoy.downstream_idle_timeout` higher/unchanged, but more importantly set `proxy_buffering off` on the edge NGINX for /v1/chat route to avoid buffering  (for customers behind NGINX proxies).
- revert the recent `http2_initial_stream_window_size` tweak if we see improvement.

We should also ask customers to try with `curl -N` (they already use -N) and `curl --no-buffer` and confirm same.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: runtime config canary for chat-gen with `batch_flush_delay_ms=50` -> canary to 5% in us-west-2 at 2026-03-11T14:20Z if approved.

eva_product: Quick question — is this strictly a streaming plumbing problem or could model quantization / kernel scheduling be affecting token generation cadence? Carol?

carol_runtime: Good call. We recently landed a quantization kernel that changed attention kernel scheduling in rare cases; however CPU/GPU generation latency per token didn't change in offline tests. The pattern here (first chunk immediate, small pause, then downstream chunking) strongly points to flush/batching heuristics rather than model compute.

alice_support: Action list (short-term):
1) carol_runtime -> create canary with `batch_flush_delay_ms=50` for chat-gen pool (5% canary us-west-2) — ETA 30m.
2) bob_sre -> set proxy buffering off on edge for /v1/chat for hosted tenants (rollback ready) — ETA 45m.
3) support -> ask customer to reproduce with trace id after canary and confirm impact; provide `x-redwood-mode: sync` header as temporary workaround to get non-streaming latency parity.

Assigning: carol_runtime, bob_sre, alice_support.

dave_acme: Appreciate it. We'll test once you announce the canary. Any quick repro tweaks we can try while you roll?

bob_sre: Repro tips for customers:
- use `curl -N --no-buffer` or Node fetch with `{ highWaterMark: 1 }` to avoid client-side buffering.
- set `Accept: text/event-stream` or use our SSE client.
- send a short prompt so responses produce multiple small chunks (repro more visible).
- include `x-request-id` header we provided so we can correlate.

Example Node repro snippet:

```
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer x', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-large-open-2026', prompt: 'short', stream: true })
});
res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()));
```

carol_runtime: Canary deployed to 5% in us-west-2 — `batch_flush_delay_ms` restored to 50 for chat-gen. I also added a temporary flag `flush_small_chunks=true` behind a kill switch. Monitoring metrics now (token inter-arrival histograms).

bob_sre: Edge proxy change applied to /v1/chat: `proxy_buffering off` on NGINX pool. Rolling back if we see noise.

alice_support: Customer confirms after canary: p95 dropped from ~4.8s -> ~550ms for streamed paths, p99 improving but still under observation. They also tested non-streaming and saw similar numbers to streamed with fixes.

dave_acme: Confirmed — big improvement. Thanks. Any longer-term plans to avoid trade-off between cost-reductions and streaming SLA?

eva_product: Long-term proposals:
- make streaming flush heuristics service-configurable with SLO-backed defaults (so Dedicated customers can tune aggressively).
- add runtime adaptive flushing: detect small burst patterns and lower timer dynamically per-session.
- expose `x-redwood-streaming-hint` header for customers to request lower-latency flush behavior (opt-in per request).
- add benchmarks that measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming vs sync in CI gating for any batching/quantization changes.

carol_runtime: We'll also add a telemetry alert: if token inter-arrival 2nd-token-to-last-token p95 > 200ms for chat-gen routes, open a pager to eng-runtime for investigation.

alice_support: Closing loop: customer happy for now. We'll keep the canary 5% -> 50% -> 100% over next 4 hours if telemetry stays green. If anything regresses, rollback plan is known.

dave_acme: Excellent. Please tag me on the rollout updates.

bob_sre: Noted. Will post rollback logs and final configs in this thread when the rollout completes.

carol_runtime: Rollout to 100% complete at 2026-03-11T18:10Z; final check shows stable p95. Leaving `flush_small_chunks` feature behind a kill switch for 24h before unguarded release.

alice_support: Marking resolved for support. If customer reopens, we will escalate. :thumbsup:
